resource_budget.output_bound_note: Every phase emits aggregate counters plus a bounded number of witness records. No per-element, per-tuple or per-point stream exists, so total run output is kilobytes. This is a deliberate departure from EXP-FROB-d8aa37 stage0, whose per-tuple stream produced a 2.44 GB partial artifact that exceeded the 100 MiB hosting limit and was never checkable.

panel.lattice_cells_note: Includes the non-semisimple cells p | n -- (3,3), (3,4)? no: (2,6),(2,4),(3,3) -- where T^n-1 is NOT squarefree, so the divisor lattice is not a Boolean lattice. The orbit census is scoped to gcd(q,n)=1 and is skipped on those cells by the driver, which records the skip.
panel.census_cells_note: Composite n (15, 21, 8, 9) carry intermediate orbit lengths dividing n and are the cells where the two derivations could most easily part company.
panel.curve_cells_note: (q, n, dim of the stable subspace V). Each dim is attainable at its (q,n). Two ordinary subfield curves of distinct j per cell where available.
panel.m_cap_note: max_m_with_net_win is searched only up to this cap, so a reported value equal to the cap means 'at least the cap', not 'exactly the cap'. Reported as such.
targets: q = 4 comparison at the same n
q = 8 comparison at the same n

preregistered_predictions.statement: Methods A (monic divisors of T^n-1), B (sigma-closure of single vectors), C (exhaustive subspace enumeration) and O (direct orbit iteration) agree exactly on every lattice cell, including the non-semisimple cells with p | n.
preregistered_predictions.falsified_if: any cell disagrees in subspace count, dimension spectrum, or orbit-length census

preregistered_predictions.statement: The annihilator/totient derivation and the Burnside derivation of the orbit census agree on every stable subspace of every census cell.

For E/F_q and V sigma-stable, F_V is pi-stable; for a random non-stable V' of the same dimension F_{V'} is not; and for a curve over F_{q^n} lying over no proper subfield there is no pi-action on F_V at all.
preregistered_predictions.falsified_if: a stable V gives a non-pi-stable factor base, or a control passes

preregistered_predictions.statement: EXACT COUNT. For n an odd prime the number of pi-orbits on F_V is exactly f + (|F_V| - f)/n, where f is the number of affine points of E(F_q) inside F_V. Equivalently every non-E(F_q) orbit has length exactly n.
preregistered_predictions.falsified_if: measured orbit count differs from the predicted count on any curve cell

preregistered_predictions.statement: At q = 2, n in {131, 163} the only faithful stable subspaces have dimension n-1, so for every m in the panel the stable factor base is inflated by more than a factor n and the orbit trick is a NET LOSS. At n in {41, 43, 127, 233} there exist m for which it is a net win.
preregistered_predictions.falsified_if: a net win appears at n = 131 or n = 163, or no net win exists at n = 127

claims.note: No discrete logarithm is solved, no relation is claimed, no deployed curve is an instance. Every measurement is an exact finite structural census, so the solution-certificate gate in docs/claims-and-verification.md does not apply. Claim tier: structural/exact, scoped to the (q, n) cells actually enumerated and to the Gaudry/Diem factor-base family F_V = {P : x(P) in V}.
